about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint James the Apostle” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: I think that God has displayed us apostles as the last, as men destined for death; for we have become a spectacle for the world, and for angels, and for men. We are fools on account of Christ, but in Christ you are prudent; we are weak, while you are strong; you are renowned, while we are obscure. Up to this hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are beaten with fists, and have no settled home, and labor, working with our hands; we are cursed, and we bless; we suffer persecution, and we endure it; we are slandered, and we beseech; we have become like the sweepings of this world, the scrapings of all, until now. It is not to shame you that I write these things, but I warn you as my beloved children. For even if you should have ten thousand guardians in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers. For it was I who begot you through the gospel in Christ Jesus.
